headline: The >100 MiB encode OOM is a single encoder-side allocation bug in propose_rle: it built a (u8,u64) run list (~16 bytes/run, ~16x the input) BEFORE its max_graph_ops decline check, so a 409 MB incompressible PDF OOM-killed the encoder before the candidate could decline. Streaming the count/longest-run in a first O(1)-memory pass and building ops only after the check removes the pathology: nasa-pdf-0001 now completes byte-exactly, and peak RSS on the 217-308 MB PDFs drops ~2x.
confirmed_prior_state: Reproduces evidence/campaigns/2026-10-08-phase16-packed-full-0b21928 rcs: nasa-pdf-0001 encode OOM (rc 137), nasa-pdf-0002/0003 encode timeout at 180 s (rc 124).

method.bisection: encode --force KIND per candidate family under /usr/bin/time -v in the capped doc-baseline lane (per-candidate peak attribution).
method.attribution_proof: 0001 --force raw completes (rc 0, 2.29 GiB, exact) while 0001 --force rle OOMs (rc 137, 6.28 GiB, 0.54 s) — RLE is the OOM locus.
method.identity_gate: before-vs-after binary differential: every corpus doc <20 MB (73) plus 0024/0020/0003/0002 (4) must produce a byte-identical .voldoc SHA-256.

bisection_release_nasa_pdf_0024_16851311.note: rle peaks ~16.6x input (2,788,964 KB) and then DECLINES (rc 2, 'candidate Rle is not proposed'). Arithmetic: observed rss - input = 2,624,401 KB = 2,687,386,624 B / 16 B = 167,961,664 runs for a 168,513,117-byte input (mean run length 1.003). Every other kind stays <= ~1 GB. auto's 2.95 GB peak is the RLE term.

root_cause.detail: let mut runs: Vec<(u8,u64)> = Vec::new(); for &b in input { ... runs.push((b,1)) ... } runs the length of `input` for near-incompressible data (16 B/run growing geometrically), and only then checks runs.len()*2 > max_graph_ops (DEFAULT 1<<20). A 409 MB PDF needs ~16.4 GB for that Vec and is SIGKILLed under the 6 GiB cap before the decline can happen.

fix.summary: Two-pass streaming propose_rle: pass 1 counts maximal runs and the longest run in O(1) memory; the max_graph_ops and max_repeat_count/u32 declines happen there; pass 2 builds the ops only when admitted (bounded by max_graph_ops/2 <= 524,288 ops). Same ops, same descriptor bytes, same decline verdict for every input.
fix.behaviour_preservation: identical candidate set/order/bytes for all inputs; verified empirically (see identity_gate).
fix.residual: peak is now ~8.9x input (was ~17.7x), spread across the decoder round-trip of the whole-file candidates (RAW/rANS/PDF_CHANNELS) and the input buffer; that is the court's decode-before-commit cost, not an unbounded structure. nasa-pdf-0001 fits under the 6 GiB cap; nasa-pdf-0002/0003 now OOM-free but still exceed the 180 s op budget on the slow BYTE_RANS lane (wall, not memory).

nasa-pdf-0002.note: wall timeout; memory no longer the cause

nasa-pdf-0003.note: wall timeout; memory no longer the cause

before_after_peak_rss.ratio_note: peak/input: before 17.68x (0003) and 17.76x (0002); after 8.97x (0003) and 8.94x (0002). Forced RLE: 15.4x OOM -> 1.006x decline.

identity_gate.conclusion: no .voldoc byte changes for any document that already encoded (77/77 identical SHA-256).

gates.phase1_receipt: raw/phase1-court/receipt.json (gate's own dated dir folded under this campaign)

open_items: nasa-pdf-0002 (228 s) and nasa-pdf-0003 (233 s) still exceed the court's 180 s op budget on BYTE_RANS; this is an encode-speed gap, distinct from the memory pathology now fixed.

Residual ~8.9x peak is the whole-file candidate round-trip (serialize -> parse -> materialize) plus the input buffer; a bounded reduction would need streaming materialization/comparison in the court, out of scope here.
The court's 180 s op budget is unchanged; raising it is a deliberate act and was not done.
